proposals: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish what the oil marketing companies' procurement systems already record for each ethanol batch — feedstock, distillery and blend grade, so it is clear whether the traceability proposed in academic blockchain papers is a real gap or already exists.

The National Sugar Institute should run and publish independent mill-level trials of AI process-control tools, measuring sugar recovery and steam use against a season-level baseline, so vendor claims such as a 0.5–1.2 point recovery gain are tested before mills invest on their strength.

The Maharashtra Agriculture Department should publish an evaluation of the Jalna district AI advisory pilot that compares participating farmers with a matched group of non-participants, so the claimed 10–20 per cent yield gain and 20–30 per cent water saving can be checked.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish monthly ethanol volumes sold by state and blend grade as E22–E30 and E85 fuels roll out, so the move beyond a single E20 mandate is tracked publicly as the system grows more complex.
